notes:
This is a beta version, published only on the beta update channel. It brings Backups, the new section that
backs up the files and the system image of the endpoints with an agent, which carries the Beta mark; the Warehouse
and Day to day improvements (each person's ID, the handover desk and collecting on someone else's behalf), ready to
use; notifications by WhatsApp and push, also in beta; histories with every module; and the license by modules, with 7
days of grace for all of them.

Before updating, make a backup and keep it (*Administration → System & updates → Backups*). This version changes
the database, and that backup is the safe way back (see *Keep in mind* at the end).
If NetPilot is behind two chained proxies (a CDN and an nginx) and trusts anyone (*), switch to a list of
proxies first: also in *Keep in mind*. A server on the stable channel is not offered this version: to get it, choose
the beta channel in *Administration → System & updates → Updates*.

The Beta mark means the same as in 1.8.3: the feature works and you can use it as usual, but it has not passed
final verification yet, so some details may still change. It is only a notice: it doesn't limit anything or change how
the feature behaves. The *Beta features* help article shows where it appears.

Backups (Beta)

- Where: the Backups section of the menu
  (Summary, Endpoints, Runs, Policies, Targets, Restore, Keys and media and Settings), with the mark
  in the menu, in the header of each page and in the help. Not to be confused with
  *Administration → System & updates → Backups*, the backup of the NetPilot server itself.
- What it backs up: the files and the system image of the endpoints with the NetPilot agent, on Windows and Linux.
  Each endpoint encrypts its backups (AES-256-GCM) before they leave it, deduplicates and compresses them, and resumes
  whatever gets interrupted. NetPilot keeps the catalog, never the contents.
- Targets: a NAS over SMB or NFS, an S3-compatible bucket (AWS, Wasabi, Backblaze, MinIO…), a folder on the
  NetPilot server or a disk of the endpoint itself, also USB disks taken in turns. Each target says which protection
  has been checked (Immutable, with S3 object lock, or Append-only verified), and endpoints only append: the
  server prunes what is no longer needed, with 30 days of quarantine.
- Policies: templates (Fixed workstations, Laptops, Servers and Weekly image only), paths and exclusions
  with snapshots (VSS on Windows), frequency and window, conditions (battery, metered connection, active user),
  retention with a preview, maximum and minimum number of backups, a bandwidth limit by time slots and
  a Second target for the 3-2-1 rule. They are assigned to each endpoint or through the RMM agent policy.
- Restore: browse a backup with search and versions, download a file or a ZIP, and restore in place, to another
  folder or to another endpoint, or revert the selection to the state of that backup. If the endpoint is off, the
  restore waits for it.
- System image: block-level incrementals (VSS on Windows and LVM on Linux), a check after each image, Deep check
  and periodic restore tests.
- Whole endpoint: Restore the whole endpoint guides the restore from the recovery media with the NetPilot
  Recovery client, connected to NetPilot with a restore key or, without the server, with the recovery kit, reading the
  NAS or the S3 bucket directly.
- Recovery media: a live Debian USB drive, with Secure Boot, served by NetPilot from Keys and media, and, if you
  prefer, a WinPE USB drive made with the New-NetPilotRecoveryMedia.ps1 script (NetPilot doesn't distribute WinPE).
  Both load drivers with Load drivers. For a Windows that is already on the disk, also one restored earlier or with
  the other medium, there are Add drivers to this Windows, Activate the Windows disk drivers (only if you choose
  it), Repair Windows boot (only with the WinPE USB drive) and Undo the last change, which goes back to the copy
  of the registry kept before changing it.
- Assistant to create the USB drive (Windows): a small program that downloads the media from your NetPilot, checks
  its signature and writes it to the USB drive without Rufus. For the WinPE USB drive it silently installs the
  Microsoft ADK if it is missing and, before creating anything, shows its license inside its own window to accept it.
  It isn't signed yet: see *Keep in mind*.
- Keys: one copy key per company, shown only once in the Backup recovery kit, with optional escrow (in the vault
  or with a passphrase) and rotation; and restore keys per endpoint, which expire and can be revoked.
- Monitoring: the Summary shows what is Protected, At risk or Unprotected in each company and the steps to
  get started; alerts for failed or overdue backups, possible ransomware (which holds back pruning), unreachable or
  full targets and failed restore tests, which can open a ticket; a daily summary, a monthly PDF report and the
  month's usage as CSV; the Backups tab on the endpoint page, its column in the inventory, the dashboard card and
  backups and restores in Latest activity.
- Space on the target, in two steps: Free up space forgets what retention no longer needs and compacts, also
  with a full target, and can be undone for 30 days; Delete now for good is a separate button that can't be undone.
- Offboarding a company from Backups, in five steps that each ask you to confirm your identity: while it still has
  backup data, the company can't be deleted.
- License and permissions: Backups is a license module, with seats per endpoint, and it also needs RMM. It has its
  own permissions (view, open backups, download, run, restore, assign policies, manage and manage targets); by default
  the reader only views and the editor has all of them except the two manage ones.

Also in beta

- WhatsApp channel: notifications over WhatsApp with Meta's official API or with Twilio, chosen when you create
  the channel in Notifications › Channels. Each person turns it on with their consent, confirming their number, and
  opts out whenever they want. Deleting the channel or changing its type, provider or sending number pauses it for
  whoever had it on: they get a notice in the bell and have to turn it on again, and NetPilot says first how many
  people it affects. It needs a public HTTPS address, a business number, an approved template and an account with the
  provider, which charges for each message.
- Push notifications: notifications on the phone or the computer even with NetPilot closed,
  with Turn on for this device (up to 10 per person). If a device's browser renews its subscription, the new one
  replaces the old one and doesn't take up another of the 10. On iPhone, with iOS 16.4 or later and NetPilot installed
  on the home screen. It needs HTTPS with a trusted certificate.
- Three-view history: the new Compact view, with only what changed and one line per change, is now the
  default; Line and Detail are still there, and your choice is remembered on all your devices.
- Latest activity on the endpoint, with what every module records: faults, check lists, licenses, planned changes,
  documentation, journal and attachments, and from the Warehouse also transfers and returns.

New in Warehouse and Day to day

- Each person's ID: a code with its QR that tells who is coming to collect material, and that gives access to
  nothing. Everyone shows theirs from My ID, on mobile also offline, and downloads it as a PDF card. A Warehouse
  manager prints the cards, for one person or in bulk, from People and permissions, and Read an ID tells whose it
  is.
- Collecting on someone else's behalf: when requesting, Who is taking it? lets you authorize who can collect it,
  also someone from outside. At the Handover desk (Deliver), the person in charge scans or looks up whoever comes
  and NetPilot says whether they can take it; if they aren't authorized, approval is requested without leaving the
  desk. It records who it was handed to, on whose behalf and who handed it out, and notifies the requester, who can
  answer It wasn't me. Earlier handovers say they have no such record.
- To collect: what is waiting for you in the warehouse shows up in My ID, on the Warehouse home, on the
  dashboard and in Today. Whoever hands out or approves has their part on the Warehouse home (To hand out
  and Asked at the counter) and their button on the mobile bar.
- The item's history and its movements show the same as the request: who requested, who approved, who handed it
  out and who collected it, with the link to the request.
- Managers by department: a person in charge limited to some departments only sees and hands out the requests of
  the warehouses of those departments. A warehouse with requests can no longer be deleted: it is deactivated.

New across the application

- How they reach me: in Notifications › How they reach me, each person chooses which notifications they receive
  over WhatsApp, push and email (Nothing, Only mine, Mine and what is important, Everything I can see
  or Custom), with Quiet hours during which critical notices still get through. It applies to every NetPilot
  notification; personal email goes out through the organization's email channel.
- Change log: Audit › Change log now collects the changes of the modules (Warehouse, Day to day, RMM, Backups
  and the rest), not only the inventory's, with secrets masked, filters by module, object type, action, user, dates
  and text, and CSV. An administrator can turn on Retention, off by default.
- A person's history: What they have done and Changes to their user in *Administration → Users*, for
  administrators; the History on their page in People and permissions, for Warehouse managers; and My activity,
  in your profile.
- License by modules: *Administration → License* shows each module with its status and how much of each quantity
  is used (11 of 25). If the license expires or is deactivated, or a module is removed or left without a quantity,
  everything keeps working for 7 days in every module, RMM included, with notices on days 1, 4 and 7; on day 7
  that module stops, without deleting anything, and comes back when you renew. Above a quantity nothing is deleted,
  but you can't add more.
- Tabs: in tab bars, whatever doesn't fit moves to More ▾ and the active tab always stays in view, on desktop
  and on mobile. The RMM tabs are now ordered by use.
- Search: the search at the top (Ctrl+K) also finds Warehouse items (by name, SKU, EAN, model or reference), units
  by serial number and requests by their code or by who made them; pasting a label's QR opens that label.

What changes

- The real IP behind a proxy: everything that looks at the IP (RMM and Backups activity, the Credentials access
  log, the attempt limits and each agent's IP) now takes the last hop, the one your proxy adds. On Docker, the
  new NETPILOT_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS variable in .env says which proxies to trust; without it, it stays *. On
  Windows, trusted_proxy now works as on Linux.
- Attempt limits: they count an IPv6 address by its /64 network, and sign-in also counts failures by email and /48
  block (100 in 10 minutes).
- Departments: whoever is limited by site, company or department no longer sees or launches in Automation what
  touches devices they can't see, doesn't see or add objects from another department in Change management and can't
  send another site's configuration to the AI analysis. Configuration backups follow their device, and compliance
  rules can only be changed by users without limits. The low or out-of-stock notice that adds up all the warehouses no
  longer reaches anyone with limits, and a warehouse's own notice only reaches those limited by department if they
  also see the item. For anyone with limits, the change log, the audit report (also when scheduled), the AI assistant
  and the time machine no longer show the history of a deleted object whose id a new one has reused.
- Password: changing yours signs out your other sessions right away, also the RMM remote ones, and those devices
  stop receiving your push notifications.
- Sessions in several tabs: when the session ends or changes person in one tab of the browser, the other tabs
  notice at once.
- Bulk changes on SQLite, the default database: editing or deleting in bulk, assigning departments and accepting
  several Discovery findings take turns with the other changes instead of failing halfway. After about 15 seconds they
  stop, keep what they did and return the rest as not processed, to run again.
- Discovery: two adoptions of the same hosts at the same time (a double click, two editors, a rule after a scan)
  no longer add them twice.
- Amber: most texts in amber (warnings, things pending) are darker and easier to read in light mode, and what goes
  on an amber background, such as the counters of the mobile bar and the offline notice, now has dark text in both
  themes.

Keep in mind

- Chained proxies: if you have two (a CDN and an nginx) with *, switch to a list of proxies before updating.
  From this version on, the limits count together everyone arriving through the first proxy, and whoever fails on
  purpose would block that account, new agents and downloads by code for all of them. On Docker,
  with NETPILOT_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS; on Windows or Linux, turn off trusted_proxy in the installer and
  set NETPILOT_TRUSTED_PROXY and NETPILOT_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS with netpilotctl config set. Also close the direct
  connection to NetPilot's port: with the proxy on the same server, NETPILOT_HTTP_PORT=127.0.0.1:8090 in the
  Docker .env. All of it in docs/OPERACION, §12.1.
- The backup recovery kit, and Kits (ZIP), need the
  *Manage policies, copy keys, seats, settings, adoptions and the trash* permission on the whole company: whoever only
  views Backups doesn't get them. Keep the kit outside NetPilot: it is what lets you recover the backups without the
  server.
- Agents: Backups needs this version's agent on each endpoint; with an older one, the endpoint
  shows Update the agent and uses no seat. 1.8.3 agents update themselves according to their agent policy, and you
  can bring it forward from the Agent versions card in *RMM → Agents*. Agents from 1.8.2 or earlier are moved once
  with Move to 1.9: despite its name, that button installs this server's version (1.8.4).
- License: Backups needs a license that includes it, with seats, and RMM. Current licenses keep working, but they
  don't include the new modules, except Enterprise, which includes them all. *Administration → License* already shows
  those of upcoming versions too (Microsoft 365, Awareness and VPN), which don't do anything yet. When renewing with
  fewer seats, the last endpoints to join Backups are left without a seat and stop backing up.
- Backups on real hardware: Backups and the recovery media haven't been tested on physical machines yet (USB
  drives, Secure Boot, BitLocker, NAS or S3 with object lock). Run a restore test before relying on a backup.
- The USB assistant isn't signed: SmartScreen will say "Windows protected your PC" (*More info → Run anyway*).
  Before opening it, compare its SHA-256 hash with the one in SHA256SUMS.txt of the release.
- WhatsApp and push have only been tested with simulated providers: the first real test is with your Meta or
  Twilio account and your devices.
- Warehouses without a department: give each warehouse its department before limiting a person in charge by
  departments; otherwise they stop seeing it and its stock notices.
- Going back from this version: if the database is downgraded, what 1.8.3 doesn't understand is lost. From
  Backups, everything NetPilot keeps (policies, targets with their credentials, keys, history and restore keys); what
  is on the targets isn't touched. From the Warehouse and notifications, the IDs, the authorized people and the record
  of who took what, the WhatsApp and push channels with their contacts and devices, the choices in How they reach me
  and the history view.
- My ID offline: the phone has to have opened NetPilot after the update; installed on the home screen it works
  better.
- Manual: the PDF manual is still the 1.8 edition and doesn't cover Backups; the in-app help already does.

Coming in the next versions (this may change)

- 1.8.5 beta, Microsoft 365 and Awareness. Connects each company's Microsoft 365: people, mailboxes, groups,
  licenses, MFA and forwarding. Actions with confirmation: block, sign out of sessions, change the password and
  "Compromised account". Backups of whatever you choose: mail, calendar, contacts, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams
  chats and channels. Simulated phishing campaigns against your own staff, courses with a certificate and a "Report"
  button.
- 1.8.6 beta, VPN and labels. NetPilot's own VPN: access to the panel, the agents' VPN, users and rules, and
  tunnels between sites. In the Warehouse: batches and expiry dates, direct printing on Zebra and TSC printers, and
  redirectable QR codes.
- 1.9.0, the final version: the complete manual and the move to the stable channel.
